Process gene data for enrichment

Source: R/jamenrich-er-methods.R
process_genedata.Rd

Process gene data for enrichment

Usage

process_genedata(
  genedata,
  genedata_params = list(refresh_genes = TRUE, ann_lib = "org.Hs.eg.db", handle_multiple
    = "best_each", empty_rule = "empty", ignore.case = TRUE, fold_cutoff = NULL,
    pvalue_cutoff = NULL, mgm_cutoff = NULL, apply_mgm_universe = TRUE, gene_colnames =
    c("SYMBOL", "probes", "gene", "gene_symbol", "geneid", "gene_id", "db_gene_symbol",
    "ncbi_gene"), fold_colnames = c("fold", "logFC", "lfc", "log2FC", "log2fold"),
    pvalue_colnames = c("adj.p.val", "adj.*P.*val", "FDR", "q.val|qval", "adjp",
    "padjust", "p.adjust", "p.value", 
     "pval"), mgm_colnames = c("mgm", "mean",
    "AveExpr"), tstat_colnames = c("t", "t.stat"), rank_strategy = c("signed-P",
    "t-statistic", "P-value", "log2fold"), try_list = c("SYMBOL2EG", "ACCNUM2EG",
    "ENSEMBL2EG", "ALIAS2EG"), sep = "/"),
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

genedata

list named by the Enrichment condition, where each list element contains a suitable form of data. Each 'genedata' will be tested for enrichment independently.

Expected formats:

  • character vector of genes, which represent "gene hits". Compatible with 'ORA' and cannot be used with 'GSEA'.

  • integer vector of integer signs limited to 1 or -1, named by gene. Compatible with 'ORA' and cannot be used with 'GSEA'. The sign applies directionality to genes, is used to define 'direction' in the pathway, but not used for enrichment itself.

  • numeric with scalar values, named by gene. Compatible with 'GSEA' and cannot be used with 'ORA'. The numeric value ranks the genes, and is applied to directionality of the results.

  • data.frame of gene stats, with columns: 'gene', 'pvalue', 'fold' in some conceptual form. Compatible with 'ORA' and 'GSEA'.

genedata_params

list to manage 'genedata'.

  • refresh_genes: logical whether to update gene symbols using genejam::freshenGenes()

  • ann_lib: character with Bioconductor library to use when 'refresh_genes' is TRUE.

  • handle_multiple: character string in genejam::freshenGenes(), default "best_each" uses the best match for each gene symbol per row.

  • empty_rule: character how to handle empty gene 'SYMBOL'. Default 'empty' leaves the value blank. Other options are 'original' to keep the original value, or 'na' to insert NA.

  • pvalue_cutoff,fold_cutoff: numeric thresholds used when genedata is supplied as a data.frame. It will define gene statistical hits using these thresholds. Default NULL will not apply thresholds, and will not define hits.

  • gene_colnames,pvalue_colnames,fold_colnames: character vectors with patterns used to match column names when 'genedata' contains a data.frame. These columns are required. The 'gene_colname' is used as the initial gene, and will be used when refresh_genes=TRUE.

  • tstat_colnames: character (optional) pattern for t-statistic column name when 'genedata' contains a data.frame. It is only used when rank_strategy='t-statistic'.

  • rank_strategy: character string used when genedata contains a data.frame:

    • 'signed-P' (default) uses the -log10(Pvalue) multiplied by the sign of the fold change. It produces the same rank order as using the t-statistic, useful when the 't' column is not available.

    • 't-statistic' uses the t-statistical column.

    • 'P-value' uses the -log10(Pvalue) to rank entries.

    • 'log2fold' uses the fold column to rank entries. Although a common default, we recommend the signed-P for improved resolution.

  • try_list: passed to genejam::freshenGenes() to determine which annotation methods to search when resolving to gene SYMBOL. They are handled in priority order, there 'best_each' will return the first (best) result for each input gene. When input genes are entirely integer values, they are assumed to be ENTREZID values, which skips this step.

verbose

logical whether to print verbose output.

...

additional arguments are passed to internal functions.

Value

data.frame with columns:

  • 'gene': the gene symbol

    • genedata_params$refresh_genes=FALSE (default) uses existing gene symbol from 'gene_colnames'

    • genedata_params$refresh_genes=FALSE uses 'SYMBOL' after applying genejam::freshenGenes(). Make sure to use correct 'ann_lib'.

  • 'sign': the numeric sign or scalar value:

    • entirely '1' for non-signed gene hits, cannot be used for ranked enrichment.

    • '1' or '-1' for signed gene hits, cannot be used for ranked enrichment.

    • numeric scalar values used for ranked enrichment.

  • 'hit': logical indicating whether each entry met the statistical cutoffs pvalue_cutoff and fold_cutoff when defined. When all entries are FALSE there were no cutoffs applied, and data should only be used for ranked enrichment.

  • The names are assigned using gene symbols, either as supplied or after resolution when genedata_params$refresh_genes=TRUE.

  • Finally, attribute 'compatible_method' indicates which enrichment tests are suitable.

Details

Workflow:detect_genedata_format

  • Define the gene column

  • Define the sign, use "1" for no sign

    • Calculate sign for "signed-P"

    • Use 't' for "t-statistic"

  • Refresh gene symbols to 'SYMBOL'

  • Remove entries with no 'SYMBOL'

  • Deconcatenate / Expand 'SYMBOL' with multiple genes

  • Resolve duplicate 'SYMBOL' to one row

    • Sort by absolute value of sign descending, then sign descending.

    • Retain the first observation per 'SYMBOL'

Custom parameters

Argument genedata_params controls additional options:

  • refresh_genes=TRUE enables genejam::freshenGenes() which uses Bioconductor annotations to update the current gene annotation to the current version available (to the active R session). Several arguments are passed to this function:

    • ann_lib: the core annotation library, 'org.Hs.eg.db' is default for Human; 'org.Mm.eg.db' is used for Mouse. This annotation database must be available, for example install Rat data with BiocManager::install('org.Rn.eg.db'). Alternatively, ann_lib can be a list with one or more AnnotationDbi or OrgDb objects.

    • handle_multiple='best_each': converts each gene to the best available match, using the priority order defined in try_list.

    • ignore.case=TRUE: Note that Human symbols are UPPERCASE, so for a moderate speed boost use ignore.case=FALSE. Note that Mouse by convention uses mixed case, for example "Apoe", and so for mouse and most other species, use ignore.case=TRUE.

    • empty_rule='empty': converts any unmatched entry to ” or NA so it is not retained in the output. This decision prevents keeping a gene or accession which can never be recognized as an official gene during pathway enrichment analysis. Use empty_rule='original' to retain the original entry whenever the entry cannot be matched to any other annotation in try_list. Note that this decision is intended only when the pathway data also contain similar gene entries which may also not have official gene symbols.

    • try_list=c('SYMBOL2EG', 'ACCNUM2EG', 'ENSEMBL2EG', 'ALIAS2EG'): is the recommended order of sources to use when equating a gene symbol or identifier with Bioconductor gene annotations. They are attempted in order, to convert each entry to an ENTREZID ('EG').

      • When using handle_multiple='best_each', each method in try_list is attempted, in order, for each gene entry, and the first successful result is retained as one or more ENTREZID values for each input gene.

      • Specifically, when 'SYMBOL2EG' is successful, it is used. Only when 'SYMBOL2EG' is not successful, 'ACCNUM2EG' is attempted. Only when 'ACCNUM2EG' is also unsuccessful, 'ENSEMBL2EG' is used, and so on.

      • The lowest priority is 'ALIAS2EG' since this association has the lowest confidence for association, and is most prone to multiple associations. In general pathway enrichment is somewhat tolerant to such lower-confidence associations, in return for having more potential opportunities for the correct association.

      • Finally, the matching ENTREZID values are converted to 'SYMBOL' so the "official gene SYMBOL" is associated with the original gene entry.

      • For each gene result, only the first unique 'SYMBOL' is retained, after applying the rank/sort operation. Typically the most significant result is retained for each gene.

      • In the event two gene identifiers are converted to the same 'SYMBOL', only the first unique 'SYMBOL' is retained, after applying the rank/sort operation. Typically, the most significant result is retained for each gene.

      • In the event one gene identifier is converted to two 'SYMBOL' values of equivalent priority, the both 'SYMBOL' values are retained, by splitting the row into multiple rows which each contain one 'SYMBOL' entry. Then the 'SYMBOL' entries overall are sorted as described above, and the first unique 'SYMBOL' is retained. Typically, the most significant result is retained for each gene.

  • gene_colnames: vector of columns that could be recognized to contain gene symbols or identifiers.

  • pvalue_cutoff, fold_cutoff: used to define gene hits when 'genedata' is data.frame. When not supplied, data can only be used for ranked enrichment.

  • mgm_cutoff: applied to max group mean (mgm) values to require each gene hit to involve one group mean of at least this value.

  • apply_mgm_universe: When TRUE it restricts the gene universe to genes with max group mean (mgm) of at least this value.
